lessons.title: Transformation controls
lessons.text: Bacteria, a plasmid, antibiotic selection, and GFP are represented as concepts. DNA can be expressed through RNA to protein; fluorescence is viewed under excitation.

lessons.title: Selection is not a census
lessons.text: Growth on antibiotic-containing medium is an observation in this fictional model. It does not show that every cell was transformed.

lessons.title: Induction is separate
lessons.text: The PBAD/AraC teaching diagram represents arabinose-associated induction of GFP expression. Ampicillin resistance is a separate plasmid function.

lessons.title: Evidence limits
lessons.text: A missing fluorescent signal does not alone establish absence of GFP DNA. A phenotype can support several possible causes.
